correctness.rationale: The three NEC votes reduce exactly to a four-symbol column map: a uniform column freezes and a discordant column copies east. A uniform column persists, while every discordant run next to an anchor erodes one position per step, proving all recurrent classes and the sharp n-1 entry bound. Cyclic change-point columns are necessary and sufficient initial anchors for convergence to a given uniform target, yielding 3^(n-b) or 3^n-2^n. Marked-anchor bounded gap compositions prove exact E_n(t), and standard union/lower independent block probability bounds prove typical log_2 n entry. The stdlib verifier enumerates all 87376 states for n=2,...,8 using the original majority vote and tests reduced update, orbit periods, basins and depths; finite checks support but do not prove all n.

value.rationale: The exact finite-width phase structure of a classical erosion rule is a natural dynamical question: all 2^n uniform patterns are fixed, all 2^n discordant patterns travel without outside basins, and fixed basin sizes depend exactly on cyclic interface count. The complete entrance-time distribution, exponential suppression of consensus basins, and sharp linear-worst/logarithmic-typical time contrast provide structural information not conveyed by a generic finite-state algorithm. The feature is not a single artificial numerical slice but holds for every circumference n>=2.
